items.stem: A team must score 150,000 document requests overnight with batch pricing. No request needs an answer at once, and each request is under 1 KB. Each batch must stay within the documented limits. Which plan meets the constraint?
options: Send all 150,000 requests in one batch, since a batch can hold them all.
Send the 150,000 requests one at a time through the synchronous Messages API overnight.
Split the job into two batches, each under 100,000 requests, and collect both result sets.
Set the batch expiry to 29 days so all 150,000 requests finish in time.
items.rationale: A batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever limit comes first. Two batches of 75,000 requests of 1 KB each stay under both limits and keep batch pricing.
items.trap: One batch for everything looks simplest, but a batch holds at most 100,000 requests or 256 MB.

items.stem: A contract pipeline extracts party names first, then computes the fee from those names. A wrong name in step one would change the fee in step two. The team must stop a wrong name before step two runs. Which design meets the constraint?
options: Run the name step and the fee step in parallel, so both finish sooner.
Check the party names in code after the fee step, and route each fee to a reviewer.
Turn on compaction, which removes wrong party names from earlier turns.
Check the party names in code before the fee step, and stop the chain at a failed check.
items.rationale: The fee step depends on the name step, so a code check between the steps catches a wrong name at its source. A stop at the failed check keeps the wrong name out of step two.
items.trap: Compaction looks like a cleanup step, but it writes a summary of older turns and does not validate values.

items.stem: A team has 80,000 review texts for overnight scoring. A live widget scores one text while a user types. The team must keep each path on the right API. Which two options meet the constraint?
options: Send the live widget requests through a batch, so each score costs less.
Split the overnight texts into batches of 256 requests, since a batch holds 256 requests.
Send the overnight texts as one Message Batch, since the batch holds up to 100,000 requests.
Send the live widget requests through the synchronous Messages API, one call per text.
items.rationale: A batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, and its results come after processing. A live widget needs each answer while the user types, so it uses the synchronous API.
items.trap: The number 256 looks like a request count, but it is the 256 MB size limit of a batch.
